title: Accelerating Material Discovery for Metal Organic Frameworks using Large Language Models
experiments_summary: The study employed a two-phase methodology. In Phase 1 (Continual Pre-Training), the Granite 3.3 2B Instruct model was continually pre-trained on multiple chemical corpora combinations: (1) PMC MOF-related articles only, (2) PubChem structural dataset only (500K compounds), (3) PMC articles combined with PubChem 500K compounds, and (4) PMC articles combined with PubChem 2M compounds (PubChem+). MOF-related PMC articles (28,525 total) were filtered from the PMC Open Access Subset using domain-specific keywords. Pre-training used a single H100 80GB GPU with batch size 1, sequence length 4096, and packing enabled. In Phase 2 (Supervised Fine-Tuning), the pre-trained models were fine-tuned on two benchmark datasets: the hMOF dataset (72,000 train / 15,428 validation / 15,428 test samples) targeting six gas adsorption properties (CO2 and CH4 at 0.05, 0.5, and 2.5 bar), and the QMOF dataset (5,226 train / 1,119 validation / 1,119 test samples) targeting electronic band gap in eV. MOFid strings served as prompts with target properties as outputs. SFT used batch size 16, sequence length 512, and packing disabled. To assess data efficiency, models were also fine-tuned on restricted SFT subsets of 1K, 3K, and 10K samples from both datasets. Baseline comparisons were made against CGCNN, SOAP, MOFormer, and the base Granite 3.3 2B model. Mean Absolute Error (MAE) was used as the evaluation metric, with hyperparameters selected via the validation sets.
